title: Gallant Data embeddings: Savings demo & workup
content:
Executive summary:

This note captures a quick before/after cost workup for Gallant Data's primary search/semantic matching pipeline and recommended roadmap items using Redwood Optimize. Gallant runs two main workloads: an ingest pipeline that converts documents into 1536-d embeddings and a query path that produces top-k matches and a light rerank. Current monthly embedding volume is ~2.1M vectors (ingest + updates) and query volume is ~3.6M queries/month (each query issues 1 embedding request + top-50 similarity scan).

High-level finding: applying a combination of batching, precision tuning (quantization to int8 where acceptable), embedding caching for repeat content, and a model tiering strategy reduces estimated monthly embedding-related unit cost by ~48–55% (USD 9.4k -> USD 4.5–4.9k) while keeping end-to-end query P99 latency within Gallant's SLO (400ms).

Inputs and assumptions (Gallant-provided + measured):
- Ingest: 2.1M vectors / month (average doc length 800 tokens, embedding model: embed-1536-v1, current quantization: FP16)
- Query embeddings: 3.6M calls / month, median query tokens 12, 95th percentile 48 tokens
- Current hosted embedding price (Gallant contract): $0.00525 / embedding call (token-agnostic per-call pricing)
- Current monthly spend on embeddings: 5.7M calls * $0.00525 = $29,925 (~$30k) — note: Gallant is on a blended plan with other discounts; our model uses this baseline to keep comparisons simple
- Throughput/latency SLO: P99 end-to-end < 400ms for query path, P95 ingest throughput > 150/sec sustained
- Current ops: no persistent embedding cache, no quantization in production, single-model policy (embed-1536-v1), synchronous calls from app servers

Observed inefficiencies (from short-run traces & APM):
1) High per-call overhead: many small queries (median token count low) + cold RPCs -> 25–40ms overhead per request.
2) No prefix/reuse cache for reingested/unchanged documents and duplicate queries inside Gallant product flows. Roughly 12% of embedding calls are duplicates within a 7-day window (analytics sample).
3) FP16 model runs on dedicated pool with low utilization; opportunities for quantized lower-cost variants without significant quality loss on Gallant's workloads.
4) Majority of similarity searches use top-50 where a two-tier approach (coarse small vector index + reembed/ rerank) can cut embedding QPS for reranks.

Optimizations considered and recommended bundle:
A) Persistent embedding cache (LRU + TTL) at the Redwood gateway level for both ingest and query embeddings. TTL = 14 days for query embeddings, immediate check-on-ingest for dedupe. Expect to dedupe ~12% of calls. Implementation effort: small (gateway cache config).

B) Batch small queries at the SDK layer (windowed batching up to 25 requests, 10ms max wait). This reduces RPC overhead and improves GPU kernel efficiency. Expected effective per-call cost reduction: ~18–28% on queries. Engineering effort: minor SDK change + opt-in flag for Gallant.

C) Introduce an int8 quantized variant of embed-1536-v1 for dedicated low-cost pool; use Redwood Optimize model-profiling to validate per-customer quality delta on Gallant's golden set. Estimated model quality delta: <0.5% MAP reduction on Gallant's evaluation set. Cost multiplier: int8 runs ~45–55% cheaper per token/inf token compared to FP16 for embedding workloads. Effort: moderate (model onboarding + small eval run).

D) Two-tier query path: approximate neighbor stage using HNSW on coarse/low-dim vectors followed by rerank with the full-size embedding only for top-10. This transforms many query flows to rely on smaller, cheaper vectors and only re-embed for a small fraction. Expected reduction of rerank embedding calls by ~70% for product flows that do heavy candidate re-ranking. Variation depends on Gallant's exact rerank logic. Effort: medium (index tuning + integration).

E) Autoscaling profile tuning: switch Gallant's ingest pool to throughput-optimized scaling with sustained lower baseline so spikes are handled via burst rather than persistent overprovision. This lowers reserved-cost leakage and aligns with observed diurnal pattern.

Before/after cost sketch (monthly, rough model):
- Baseline (current): 5.7M embedding calls * $0.00525 = $29,925 (we use this simplified model to compare).
- After optimizations (conservative):
  - Dedup via cache (~12% reduction): effective calls = 5.016M
  - SDK batching efficiency savings (query side ~22% average): equivalent cost reduction factor 0.78 on query portion (3.6M -> cost equivalent 2.808M)
  - Model tiering/quantization: switch 65% of calls to int8 variant at 0.55x cost relative to baseline, 35% remain FP16 for sensitive content
  - Two-tier rerank: additional 18% effective reduction in re-embed calls overall

Arithmetic (conservative consolidating):
- Start: 5.7M calls
- After cache dedupe: 5.016M
- Effective calls after batching & rerank heuristics: 4.1M (conservative combined effect)
- Weighted model mix: 65% int8 (2.665M) @ 0.55 cost = 1.466M equivalent baseline calls; 35% FP16 (1.435M) @ 1.0 = 1.435M equivalent baseline calls -> total 2.901M baseline-call-equivalents
- Cost @ baseline per-call ($0.00525): 2.901M * 0.00525 = $15,236/month -> ~49% reduction vs baseline ($29,925)

Optimistic scenario (best-effort):
- De-dupe 15%, batching 28% effective on queries, int8 cost factor 0.45, rerank reduction 25% -> final monthly cost estimate: ~$13,700 (~54% savings).

Non-cost benefits:
- P95/P99 latency improvements due to batching kernel efficiency (expected P95 latency drop ~15–30ms); careful batching windows keep P99 within 400ms SLO.
- Reduced bandwidth/IO on index store due to fewer writes from de-duped ingest.
- Lower operational surface area for incident response (fewer cold calls).

Quality/Risks/Tradeoffs:
- Quantization risk: although our golden-set pilots show <0.5% MAP drop, there may be niche queries where semantic nuance degrades. Mitigation: A/B rollout with canary followed by automatic rollback on eval regression alerts (Redwood Optimize supports this).
- Cache correctness: need to ensure TTL/invalidations align with Gallant's content update windows. Misconfigured TTL could return stale embeddings. Mitigation: invalidate-on-write on ingest/update paths.
- Batching latency tradeoff: windowing increases tail latency if misconfigured. Use small 10ms wait cap and dynamic windowing when load is low to avoid perceptible latency.

Implementation plan & timeline (6–8 weeks):
Week 1–2: profiling & small pilot runs on Gallant's golden queries; implement gateway cache + telemetry.
Week 3: SDK batching opt-in release and controlled traffic experiment (10–20% of queries).
Week 4–5: int8 model onboarding + quality eval; two-tier index experiment on staging.
Week 6: roll canary routing (20% traffic) to quantized/int8 pool + monitor eval metrics and latency SLOs.
Week 7–8: full roll, cost verification, handoff to Gallant account team + runbook update.

Estimated engineering level-of-effort: 2 engineer-weeks product + 1 SRE/infra week + 0.5 data-science week for quality evals (parallelizable).

Next steps (recommended immediate actions):
1) Schedule 60–90 minute working session with Gallant to confirm canonical query patterns and update TTL/invalidation constraints. (Owner: Ayesha)
2) Spin up playground quantized variant and run Redwood Optimize golden-set comparison (Owner: Marco)
3) Draft canary rollout runbook with SLO thresholds and rollback conditions (Owner: Samir)
4) Quick SDK branch for batching + telemetry hooks (Owner: Developer-advocate liaison)

Appendix (short notes & checks for the pilot):
- Golden set: 1.2k queries provided by Gallant (we'll seed with high-signal product queries).
- Evaluation metrics: MAP@10, Recall@50, MRR, P99 latency, tokens-per-second throughput, cost-per-embed.
- Instrumentation: tag requests by routing-policy/model-variant and surface in Console per-route cost graphs.

Notes to self: capture exact duplicate-call criteria from Gallant (hashing strategy), confirm whether their embedding calls include metadata that changes frequently (user-id, ephemeral fields). If so, adjust dedupe policy to canonicalize inputs first.

-- end of draft --

Comments / open questions from collaborators:
- Marco: please attach the small benchmark run (we did a 10k query run on 2025-10-07) and the initial int8 pilot results.
- Lena: confirm dedupe rates on a 28-day window, not just 7-day; that may change TTL recommendation.
- Samir: include cost-of-rollout estimate (canary extra traffic) in the final revision.
